figure.name: Andrew Jackson
figure.era: Jacksonian democracy, slavery, and Indian removal (1820-1845)
figure.role: U.S. president associated with Jacksonian democracy, slavery, Indian removal, territorial expansion, and state-backed dispossession.
figure.hook: Jackson = democracy for some, removal for Native nations, and land for settler expansion.
whyHere: Jackson belongs here because capitalism in America cannot be separated from land, slavery, white settlement, law, and state power.
He matters because Indian removal shows how democratic politics for settlers could become coercive dispossession for Native nations.
figure.cleanIdea: American capitalism did not expand through markets alone; it also expanded through state-backed land seizure, slavery, settler politics, and forced removal.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The Indian Removal Act exposes the American capitalism ledger: land, slavery, settler democracy, state force, and Native dispossession.

ideas.title: Removal Policy
ideas.plainDefinition: Removal policy means state action used to force Native peoples from homelands into other territories.
ideas.context: In the Jackson path, removal policy connects federal law, settler pressure, land hunger, slavery expansion, and Native dispossession.
ideas.whyMatters: Removal policy matters because American expansion was not just migration or markets. It was also law, force, and broken sovereignty.

ideas.title: Settler State
ideas.plainDefinition: A settler state uses law, force, treaties, land policy, and political institutions to secure settler control over territory.
ideas.context: In the Jackson path, the state protects settler expansion while claiming democratic legitimacy for the settler public.
ideas.whyMatters: Settler state matters because democracy for one group can become domination for another when sovereignty and land are denied.

ideas.title: Expansion Politics
ideas.plainDefinition: Expansion politics is political conflict over territorial growth, settlement, markets, slavery, sovereignty, and state power.
ideas.context: In the Jackson path, expansion politics ties land hunger to public policy and racial hierarchy.
ideas.whyMatters: Expansion politics matters because capitalist development in the United States grew inside fights over land, labor, race, and state violence.
